verdict.summary: ServiceNow is proving enterprise AI can monetize through workflow contracts rather than infrastructure spend alone. Q2 subscription revenue reached $3.877B, cRPO $13.2B and total RPO $29.0B. AI annual contract value crossed $1B, while GAAP/non-GAAP operating margins were 4%/29.5% and free cash flow was $634M. The weak point is the 25.5-point adjustment gap. FY2026 subscription guidance is $15.76B-$15.78B with 35% FCF margin, but federal revenue moved forward from Q3 and heavier AI usage may pressure gross margin. The dated framework is 9.3x guided revenue and a 3.8% guided FCF yield. A completed 15-minute close above $141.39 activates risk to the Aug. 27 low at $130.25; $160.6799 and $161.9320 are December swing highs. Contract growth must outrun infrastructure and compensation costs.

business.overview:
ServiceNow sells subscriptions that digitize IT, employee, customer, security and creator workflows. Revenue grows through seats, workflow expansion, premium editions and longer enterprise commitments. Subscription revenue, cRPO and large net-new ACV transactions reveal whether the platform is broadening inside customers.

The AI transmission channel is workflow execution. AI Control Tower, agents and data context can route, govern and complete work across departments and third-party systems. Crossing $1B of AI annual contract value makes that channel measurable, while cRPO shows whether contracts persist beyond pilot projects.

The model breaks if agents remain demos, if customers resist premium pricing, or if acquisitions and hyperscaler costs erode unit economics. Q2 included federal on-premise revenue pulled forward from Q3, which flatters near-term growth. ServiceNow must convert AI contracts into durable subscription revenue while narrowing the large GAAP/non-GAAP margin gap; otherwise a premium multiple rests on adjusted economics that owners do not fully receive.
business.moat: ServiceNow's moat is its workflow schema, configuration data, enterprise integrations and role as a system of action across departments. AI agents become more valuable when they can invoke those governed workflows, but Salesforce, Microsoft and specialist automation vendors compete for the same control layer.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: ServiceNow reported 1,034,000,000 shares outstanding at June 30, 2026 and 1,034,334,000 diluted weighted-average shares for Q2. The 1.034334B quarterly diluted average is the minimum calculable denominator; a current theoretical fully diluted count is unavailable because outstanding awards are not reconciled into one point-in-time figure. ServiceNow has approximately $4.66B cash against $8.45B debt. No ATM or prospectus supplement was reviewed. Employee equity and acquisition consideration remain the principal dilution channels; the goal to reduce stock compensation below 10% of revenue by 2029 matters because the GAAP/non-GAAP gap remains large.
